question: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in meters?
raw_answer: The Burj Khalifa is 828 metres tall. [3]

message.content: The Burj Khalifa is 828 metres tall. [3]

passages.heading: Architecture and design
passages.text: The spire of Burj Khalifa is composed of more than 4,000 tonnes (4,400 short tons; 3,900 long tons) of structural steel. The central pinnacle pipe weighs 350 tonnes (390 short tons; 340 long tons) and has a height of 200 m (660 ft). The spire also houses communications equipment.<sup>[42]</sup> This 244-metre (801 ft) spire is widely considered vanity height, since very little of its space is usable. Without the spire, Burj Khalifa would be 585 metres (1,919 ft) tall. This was reported in a Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat study, which notes that the empty spire "could be a skyscraper on its own".<sup>[2]</sup> Such a skyscraper, if located in Europe, would be the 11th tallest building on that continent.<sup>[43]</sup>

passages.heading: Milestones
passages.text:
- 1 September 2008: Height tops 688 m (2,257 ft), making it the tallest human-made structure ever built, surpassing the previous record-holder, the Warsaw Radio Mast in Konstantynów, Poland.<sup>[110]</sup>
- 17 January 2009: Topped out at 829.8 m (2,722 ft).<sup>[111]</sup>
- 1 October 2009: Emaar announces that the exterior of the building is completed.<sup>[112]</sup>
- 4 January 2010: Burj Khalifa's official launch ceremony is held and Burj Khalifa is opened. Burj Dubai was renamed Burj Khalifa in honour of the President of the UAE and ruler of Abu Dhabi, Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed al Nahyan.<sup>[4]</sup>
- 10 March 2010: Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat certifies Burj Khalifa as world's tallest building.<sup>[113]</sup>

## Awards

In June 2010, Burj Khalifa was the recipient of the 2010 "Best Tall Building Middle East & Africa" award by the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat.<sup>[158]</sup> On 28 September 2010 Burj Khalifa won the award for the best project of the year at the Middle East Architect Awards 2010.<sup>[159]</sup> Awards Chair Gordon Gill, of Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture, said:

We are talking about a building here that has changed the landscape of what is possible in architecture – a building that became internationally recognized as an icon long before it was even completed. 'Building of the Century' was thought a more apt title for it.<sup>[160]</sup>

#

The exterior cladding, comprised of aluminum and textured stainless steel spandrel panels, was designed to withstand Dubai’s extreme temperatures during the summer months by using a low-E glass to provide enhanced thermal insulation. Vertical polished stainless steel fins were added to accentuate Burj Khalifa’s height and slenderness.

The unprecedented height of the Burj Khalifa required it to be an innovative building in many ways. Design techniques, building systems, and construction practices all required rethinking, and in many cases new applications, to create a practical and efficient building.

828 metres tall, Burj Khalifa is a mixed-use skyscraper in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It ranks first among the world's tallest completed buildings by architectural height. [2]

The current Skyscraper Center lists the highest occupied floor at 585.4 metres, while the retrieved Wikidata statement lists 584.5 metres and the supplied prompt uses 585 metres. INSIDE THE ENGINEERING

How Burj Khalifa was built.

Design, structure and construction. Technical sources reviewed 9 September 2026.

SOM arranged three concrete wings around a six-sided core. Each wing braces the other two, while the central cell supplies torsional stiffness. The setback geometry aligns columns above with walls below, avoiding disruptive transfers as the floor plate reduces. Gravity and lateral resistance follow the same disciplined geometry.

A reinforced-concrete mat, 3.7 metres thick, distributes the tower load to bored piles 1.5 metres in diameter and 43 metres long. The mat was cast in four pours totalling 12,500 cubic metres. Low-permeability concrete forms part of the foundation durability strategy.

The Samsung C&T, Six Construct and Arabtec joint venture had to coordinate cranes, labour and material supply vertically. BESIX reports concrete pumping to 585 metres and cycles reaching two floors per week. Special mixes and predominantly night-time pours addressed temperatures exceeding 45°C.

Successive setbacks change the shape the wind encounters, reducing coherent vortex formation. The envelope uses silver-coated glazing to limit solar gain. Mechanical equipment is distributed through double-height service floors; the design also collects air-conditioning condensate for reuse. The steel spire was assembled inside the building and hydraulically raised into position.

passages.heading: Architecture & Design
passages.text:
## Architecture & Design

Burj Khalifa was masterfully designed by the Chicago-based architectural firm Skidmore, Owings & Merrill LLP (SOM), renowned for pioneering ultra-tall structures. Led by consulting design partner Adrian Smith, FAIA, RIBA. Inspired by Islamic architecture, its design is rooted in a harmonious Y-shaped floor plan, signifying unity and structural strength. Every phase of its creation, from the groundbreaking foundations embedded deep within the desert to the soaring structure that grew floor by floor, reflects precision, innovation, and ambition.

passages.heading: Things to Do Near Dubai Burj Khalifa
passages.text:
## Things to Do Near Dubai Burj Khalifa

Burj Khalifa‘s height, reaching an impressive 828 metres, is complemented by its 163 floors that are home to premium offices, luxurious hotels, world-class restaurants, and exclusive residences. The uppermost floors are dedicated to observation decks, providing panoramic views of Dubai. Notable features include a swimming pool on the 76th floor and a mosque on the 158th floor, both of which are the highest in the world. The Armani Dubai Hotel, housed within Burj Khalifa, is the highest hotel globally. Additionally, the Burj Khalifa Sky Lounge offers a bar and restaurant experience with breathtaking vistas.

passages.heading: Visitor Information
passages.text:
Residing in Burj Khalifa offers an unmatched lifestyle. Residents enjoy stunning views, direct access to __Dubai Mall__—the world’s most visited shopping and entertainment destination—and Dubai Fountain, the world’s largest dancing fountain. The building’s design, inspired by Islamic architecture, features a tripartite floor plan and a buttressed core, enhancing both its aesthetic appeal and structural integrity. Burj Khalifa, like other tall buildings, presents unique architectural design and engineering challenges, showcasing advancements in materials and construction techniques.

Comparing Burj Khalifa with other iconic structures like the Willis Tower and the World Trade Center highlights its architectural significance and the evolution of skyscraper design.

passages.heading: Design inspired by the desert
passages.text:
# Design inspired by the desert

The design for the Burj Khalifa combines local cultural influences with cutting-edge technology to achieve high performance in an extreme desert climate. As the centerpiece of a mixed-use development, the 162-story tower contains offices, retail space, residential units, and an Armani Hotel. The Y-shaped floor plan maximizes views of the Arabian Gulf. At ground level, the skyscraper is surrounded by green space, water features, and pedestrian-friendly boulevards.

passages.heading: Design inspired by the desert
passages.text: The design for the tower is inspired by the geometries of a regional desert flower and the patterning systems embodied in Islamic architecture. Built of reinforced concrete and clad in glass, the tower is composed of sculpted volumes arranged around a central buttressed core. As it rises from a flat base, setbacks occur in an upward spiraling pattern, which reduces the building’s mass as it reaches skyward. At the pinnacle, the central core emerges and is sculpted to form a spire.
